Risk Statement: If identities or roles have permissions beyond business need, credential compromise or operator error could enable unauthorized resource changes, data access or service disruption.
Illustrative Treatment: Review effective permissions; remove unused grants; apply least privilege; use permission boundaries or organization guardrails where appropriate.

Risk Statement: If privileged human access is not protected by strong authentication and controlled role assumption, stolen credentials could be used to administer the environment.
Illustrative Treatment: Enforce MFA for privileged human access, prefer federation and short-lived credentials, and review break-glass controls.

Risk Statement: If security groups, routes or public endpoints expose management or data services unnecessarily, external actors may reach sensitive resources.
Illustrative Treatment: Inventory public exposure; remove unnecessary paths; restrict ingress to approved sources and services.

Risk Statement: If application, administration and data tiers are not effectively separated, compromise of one component could enable lateral movement.
Illustrative Treatment: Define trust zones and data flows; restrict security-group paths; test approved and denied connectivity.

Risk Statement: If relevant management activity is not captured across the required accounts or regions, investigations may lack a reliable audit trail.
Illustrative Treatment: Validate trail coverage, event selectors, destinations and required account/region scope.

Risk Statement: If log destinations or retention controls can be altered by the same actors being monitored, security events may be concealed or unavailable.
Illustrative Treatment: Restrict log administration, protect destinations, define retention and consider log-file validation and centralized ownership.

Risk Statement: If important security events are not alerted, assigned and reviewed, detection and response may be delayed.
Illustrative Treatment: Define alert use cases, owners, escalation SLAs and periodic alert tests.

Risk Statement: If resources drift from approved baselines without detection or review, insecure settings may persist unnoticed.
Illustrative Treatment: Enable appropriate configuration recording and rules; define drift triage and exception handling.

Risk Statement: If cloud changes bypass review or approved deployment paths, errors may create exposure or disrupt critical services.
Illustrative Treatment: Use reviewed infrastructure-as-code, change approvals, deployment-role restrictions and traceable releases.

Risk Statement: If backups or recovery procedures are not adequately protected and tested, an outage or destructive event may cause prolonged service interruption or data loss.
Illustrative Treatment: Validate backup coverage, access separation, restore testing and approved RTO/RPO.

Risk Statement: If access keys or secrets are committed to source code or pipelines, unauthorized parties may obtain cloud access.
Illustrative Treatment: Prefer roles and short-lived credentials; use managed secret storage and scanning; rotate any exposed credentials.

Risk Statement: If findings and exceptions lack accountable owners, due dates or escalation, cloud risks may remain unresolved beyond tolerance.
Illustrative Treatment: Assign owners and SLAs; track exceptions and residual risk; report overdue critical/high actions.
